solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: see 11ac.
Like a blow-up doll accepted by boring bloke

blocks.note: an idea that is accepted is 'in'
flat means dull or boring
Ed stands in for any ordinary bloke

explanation.surface: A dull man has adopted a blow-up doll as a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow-up doll is filled with air, which is exactly what being inflated describes.

clue.text: Act shocked about collaring church sexual predator

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for acting shocked runs backwards
to collar someone is to grab them round the neck, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: to reel is to stagger back in shock
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone feigns outrage after a churchman is caught as a sex offender.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecher is a lustful man who pursues women, so the clue's predator label is a loose but fair synonym.

clue.text: Drip wrapping up right movie star

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the abbreviation is read from bottom to top
wrapping means one word is folded around the other

blocks.note: to drip slowly is to seep
RT is a common abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sneering critic calls a famous actor a drip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drip' looks like an insult aimed at the star, but it supplies the outer word; in a down entry 'up' reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is one of Hollywood's most celebrated actresses, an example of a film celebrity.

clue.text: Breed of fixer – retro bastard

indicators.note: a bastard is of mixed or irregular origin, so these letters are produced in a jumbled form

blocks.note: the letters of both words together are the fodder

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at an old-fashioned fixer, calling him a bastard of a breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox terrier is a recognised dog breed, originally used to flush foxes from their earths.

clue.text: Dicky feeling Nell's tits, twice taking time out for refreshment

indicators.note: time is T, and taking it out twice removes both of those letters
refreshing something renews it, so the letters are made over in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written before the deletion

explanation.surface: A lewd scene of groping, interrupted twice for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TITS without both Ts leaves IS, which joins NELLS for the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicky is British slang for unwell or weak, so a dicky feeling is a sense of being poorly.

clue.text: Given the dumbing down treatment, old-style court favoured initially by Miliband?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: to spoon is a dated word for courting or canoodling
first letter of favoured
Ed Miliband, former leader of the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: A jibe that Ed Miliband patronises voters with oversimplified politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Being spoon-fed means having everything simplified and handed over so no thinking is required.

clue.text: Give me what I want, gymnastic fashion!

blocks.note: first meaning: to provide what is needed or requested
second meaning: an adverb, in a supple, bendy manner

explanation.surface: A demanding plea from a lover to someone athletic.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the rare adverb from supple, pronounced differently from the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to provide goods or needs, while the adverb describes moving in a lithe, flexible way.

clue.text: Way to have a shag the old-fashioned way – it's a breeze

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun: a stroll is something easy

blocks.note: ST, short for street, is a way

blocks.clueFragment: to have a shag the old-fashioned way
blocks.note: a roll in the hay is a dated euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that seduction in the traditional manner is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll, or a walk in the park, is an idiom for a task achieved without effort.

clue.text: Nick, you're one southern wanker, initially ripe for replacement

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the insult before it
replacing things puts them in different positions, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
first letter of wanker
the fodder for rearranging

explanation.surface: An insult aimed at someone called Nick, branding him a southern wanker due for replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a man's name being addressed; it is the verb to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for stealing, and a swiper is a thief who grabs things.

clue.text: Start to plug middle of chef Lawson's kinky TV genre?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
the middle of a four-letter word is its central pair of letters
kinky means twisted, so these letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of plug
the central two letters of chef
Nigella Lawson, the TV cook, taken as written

explanation.surface: A smutty hint about Nigella Lawson's cookery programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel show is a television format where a group of guests answer questions, a recognised kind of programme.

clue.text: (&1dn.) Singer Jack's a fair way through "No hotel to be trashed before noon"

indicators.note: no hotel means the letter for hotel in the phonetic alphabet is dropped
a trashed room is wrecked and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, then shorn of its H
N stands for noon
Jack is a familiar form of John

explanation.surface: A singer is said to be well into a lyric about a hotel being wrecked before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotel is H in the phonetic alphabet; removing it leaves OTEL to scramble. The rock-star habit of trashing hotel rooms is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John is one of Britain's best-known pop singers and pianists, famous for his flamboyant stage performances.

clue.text: Chuck has rest disturbed – pot victim?

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of place, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: to lob is to chuck or toss
the fodder for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone called Chuck has a disturbed night, perhaps a cannabis smoker.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot suggests cannabis; here it is the trap a fisherman uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobsters are caught in baited traps called pots, so one is a creature caught that way.

clue.text: Balls, spot the alien confident state of investors!

blocks.note: bull is nonsense, like balls
a spot or blemish is a mark
ET, the film alien

explanation.surface: A dismissive retort, with someone told to spot an alien.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull market is a period of rising prices when traders feel optimistic about stocks.

clue.text: Pulp fiction? Yours is crap, nothing omitted, coming in scrolls?

indicators.note: nothing is the round letter O, and omitted says to leave it out
crap means badly made, so the remaining letters come out in a mess

blocks.note: pap is soft pulp and also trashy reading matter
taken as written, then losing O

explanation.surface: A sneering editor tells a writer their pulp novel is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus was the ancient writing material made from reeds and rolled into long scrolls.

clue.text: Rival, mid-revolution, introduced as a tough guy leader

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters before it are overturned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
introduced means put in

explanation.surface: A rival emerging during a revolution is presented as a strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-revolution' reads as one hyphenated phrase, but MID is fodder and revolution the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia's president cultivates a macho strongman image, bare-chested horse riding included.

clue.text: Rabid beast's bloody U-turn?

indicators.note: a U-turn sends you back the way you came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: goddam is an American intensifier like bloody

explanation.surface: An angry outburst at a politician's U-turn, calling them a rabid beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog infected with rabies becomes crazed and aggressive, which is the literal sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Member possibly exposed and deprived of get up and go?

definitions.text: deprived of get up and go

blocks.note: first meaning: with the trouser fly open

blocks.clueFragment: deprived of get up and go
blocks.note: second meaning: read as ..., lacking zip or energy

explanation.walkthrough: Zip is slang for energy, so the second reading splits the word as un- plus zipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening a fly can leave the penis on show, while having no zip means lacking vigour and drive.

clue.text: see 25dn.
Boris's first to measure young female's expansive region

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the name

blocks.note: first letter of Boris
an en is a printer's measure
gal is a casual word for a girl

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson sizing up a young woman's figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal is a large historical area of the Indian subcontinent, now split between India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Stony-hearted international body relocated

blocks.note: the United Nations
relocated means moved

explanation.surface: A heartless global organisation has shifted its headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unmoved shows no emotion or sympathy, which is what a cold, hard person does.

clue.text: IOU, say, which takes guts when leader's replaced

indicators.note: the leader is a word's first letter, and replacing it swaps in a different one

blocks.note: guts are the bowels

explanation.surface: An IOU that requires courage to write.
explanation.walkthrough: B gives way to V; the new letter is not separately clued. 'IOU' looks like a debt note but is just three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: I, O and U are three of the five vowel letters, so the clue offers them as an example.

clue.text: Weird casual business associated with left half of bust

indicators.note: keeping roughly the left-hand portion means the tail of the word is cut off

blocks.note: biz is informal for business
a police bust is an arrest

explanation.surface: An informal business linked to half a woman's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: Bust looks anatomical but is a police raid; ARREST loses its final ST, which is a loose 'half'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre means strange or outlandish, a direct synonym for odd behaviour or things.

clue.text: Fan Brenda – boring old fart

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose cipher is ER

explanation.surface: An admirer of Brenda is dismissed as tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Old buffer is British slang for a dull, fuddy-duddy elderly man.

clue.text: Spin worth a toss?

indicators.note: spinning sends things round, so the letters of the next word land in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder for rearranging

explanation.surface: Asking whether a spin of a coin is worth bothering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' wants to be a definition alongside 'a toss'; it is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A throw and a toss are both the act of flinging something, as with dice or a ball.

clue.text: Sick? Well, it's the sprogs

blocks.note: off means unwell, as in feeling off
a spring is a well of water

explanation.surface: A parent blames the kids for feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprogs is British slang for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are one's children, the same thing sprogs means in casual British usage.

clue.text: (&18dn.) Press screen reinstated by 15?

definitions.note: cryptic: a thing Putin is suspected of bringing back

blocks.note: to press clothes is to iron them
a curtain is a screen

explanation.surface: A fear that a Russian leader is restoring Soviet-era barriers.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 refers to the answer at 15-across, the Russian president.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cold War division of Europe was called this, and Putin is accused of wanting to rebuild that split.

clue.text: They can't be any better when vibrating ladies

indicators.note: vibrating things shake about, so these letters are jiggled into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder for rearranging

explanation.surface: A cheeky hint about ladies and vibrators being unbeatable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are perfect standards of excellence, so by definition nothing can surpass them.

clue.text: Info, e-shit and fifty collective attributes of a sexually-active group

definitions.text: collective attributes of a sexually-active group

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
taken as written
poo is excrement
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A rant about online information and spam.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene pool is the total set of inherited variation within an interbreeding population.
